title: Little Albert (Watson & Rayner, 1920)

youtube.title: They Taught a Baby to Fear a Rat. In One Week. #Shorts
youtube.description:
You're nine months old and you love the fluffy white rat. Then a loud bang starts every time you touch it.
A week later, you scream at the rat alone.

This is Watson and Rayner's 'Little Albert' study (1920), told from the inside. After seven pairings, the fear was learned, and it spread to a rabbit, a dog, a fur coat, even a Santa Claus mask. Nobody ever tried to undo it.

Which of YOUR fears were learned? Tell me in the comments.

Sources:
- Watson, J. B., & Rayner, R. (1920). Conditioned emotional reactions. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 3(1), 1-14.
- Harris, B. (1979). Whatever happened to Little Albert? American Psychologist, 34(2).

#psychology #littlealbert #conditioning #shorts #mindset

sources: Watson, J. B., & Rayner, R. (1920). Conditioned emotional reactions. J Experimental Psychology 3(1): at about 9 months Albert showed no fear of a white rat, rabbit, dog, monkey, masks, cotton wool.
Same paper: a steel bar was struck with a hammer behind his head as he reached for the rat; after seven pairings over two sessions a week apart he cried and crawled away at the rat alone.
Same paper: five days later the fear transferred to a rabbit, a dog, a sealskin fur coat, cotton wool and a Santa Claus mask.
Albert left before any attempt to remove the fear; his later identity is still disputed (Harris 1979; later identification attempts).
lines: You're nine months old. They put a soft white rat in front of you. You love it. You reach out to touch it.
Nineteen twenty, Johns Hopkins. Psychologist John Watson shows you a rabbit, a dog, a mask, cotton wool. You're not afraid of anything.
Then, every time you touch the rat, a man hits a steel bar with a hammer, right behind your head.
Bang. You jump. You fall forward. You start to cry. They do it again, and again.
After just seven bangs, they show you the rat alone. No noise at all. You scream, and crawl away as fast as you can.
Days later, the fear has spread. A rabbit, a dog, a fur coat, even a Santa Claus mask now make you cry.
Then you leave the study. Nobody ever tries to undo the fear. Who you grew up to be is still debated.
Today it's taught as a lesson in ethics. But it showed something unsettling. A fear can be learned in about a week.
Some of your fears were never really yours. They were learned. So which of yours could you unlearn?
